newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Shipley withholds view on NZ MP's clothes spend.
newsitem.headline: Shipley withholds view on NZ MP's clothes spend.

text.p: State Owned Enterprises Minister Jenny Shipley will not say whether New Zealand First MP and former Aotearoa Television director Tukoroirangi Morgan's spending on clothes (including those, by now, legendary $89 underpants) was over the top.

Shipley asked for a report on allowances normally available to television reporters and presenters which found the normal annual allowance was less than the $4000 Morgan spent in a single spending spree at Auckland's up-market Politiks clothes shop only weeks before he swapped journalism for politics.
State-owned TVNZ told Shipley it had a sliding range of allowances for reporters regularly on screen, depending on how often they appeared, from $1000 to $3000 a year.
"With the absolute maximum (set) at $3000 per annum, per reporter which covers grooming, dry-cleaning, clothing and make- up requirements," a spokeswoman for Shipley said.
If reporters wanted to purchase clothing they needed the prior approval of TVNZ and must furnish receipts.
"The clothing allowance is restricted to items that are seen on screen such as suits, ties, shirts and raincoats. It does not include shoes, underwear and jewellery."
TVNZ buys clothes for presenters to wear but they remain the property of TVNZ.

"That presenter policy does not apply to (current affairs show host) Paul Holmes who has a separate employment contract ... which TVNZ was unable to disclose for reasons of commercial confidentiality," the spokeswoman said.
She said Shipley had not drawn a conclusion in relation to spending at the Maori-language station because it was not known how much Morgan and Aotearoa director Morehu McDonald spent in a full year.
"We know how much they spent in one fell swoop, but there is a lot of detail to come on ATN yet."
The spokeswoman said Shipley did not report to cabinet on the clothing allowance issue but had discussed it informally with cabinet colleagues.
"But it was not a significant factor in their decision- making on Aotearoa TV," the spokeswoman said.
On Monday Cabinet reserved its decision to provide another $4 milllion in funding for the station in the wake of allegations of poor financial management at the station.
A Serious Fraud Office investigation into the station's affairs is underway.
